statement: Let Q be an m-element set, X an N-element set with N>=m, and F a finite family of k-tuples (f_1,...,f_k) of maps X->X, where k>=1. A tuple (delta_1,...,delta_k) of permutations of Q is represented if there are an injection E:Q->X and a tuple (f_j) in F such that f_j(E(q))=E(delta_j(q)) for every j and q. If (N)_m |F| < (m!)^k, then some permutation tuple is unrepresented. Proof: There are (m!)^k target tuples and (N)_m injections. For a fixed injection E and fixed map tuple (f_j), there is at most one target tuple satisfying the displayed equations, because for each q,j injectivity of E makes delta_j(q) unique if f_j(E(q)) lies in E(Q); otherwise there is no represented tuple. Hence at most (N)_m|F| target tuples are represented. The strict inequality implies at least one is unrepresented.

proved_step: For every n>=1 and integer s>=0, in the fan-in-two Boolean circuit model over {AND,OR,NOT} with n named inputs and one output, there is a uniform deterministic procedure that outputs a truth table outside the size-s circuit image, using at most 2^{2^n} * 2^{O((s+1)log(n+s+2))} * 2^n time and 2^{2^n} bits of working storage, provided the circuit image is proper. Proof: Enumerate every n-bit truth table in lexicographic order as a candidate. For each candidate, enumerate all circuit descriptions with at most s gates, evaluate each on all 2^n inputs, and compare its output table with the candidate. Output the first candidate unmatched by every enumerated circuit. Each gate has one of three types and at most (n+s+1)^2 ordered predecessor choices, and the output chooses among n+s+1 wires; summing over gate counts gives at most 2^{O((s+1)log(n+s+2))} descriptions. Evaluating one circuit takes O((s+1)2^n) operations. The candidate loop has 2^{2^n} iterations. Every size-s circuit is enumerated, and properness guarantees an unmatched candidate. This does not establish the CJSW-efficient refuter required by G0001 and does not close G0001.

statement_start: Let Q be an m-element set, X an N-element set with N≥m, and F a finite family of k-tuples of maps X→X. If every k-tuple of permutations of Q is represented by some injection E:Q→X and some map tuple in F, then |F|≥(m!)^k/(N)_m.
evidence: For each pair (E,f) there is at most one represented permutation tuple: for each j,q, injectivity of E determines δ_j(q) uniquely from f_j(E(q)), if that value lies in E(Q). There are (N)_m injections and |F| map tuples, so at most (N)_m|F| distinct targets are represented. Covering all (m!)^k targets forces (N)_m|F|≥(m!)^k. This is a finite counting lemma only; it does not shrink G0001's uniform efficient refuter requirement.
